assignments.brief_reason: Uses aggression/fear-inducing content and personal attacks as the main removal criteria.
Downweights posts for being mainly insults/cursing rather than substantive, fitting the toxicity/threat removal bar.
States physical violence is a deal-breaker for removal/decision.
Focuses on personal attacks and framing (with foul language) as determinants of keep vs remove, aligning with removing toxic/threatening content.
Supports free speech while disliking profanity; insufficient explicit violence/threat exception language for theme 2.
Appeals to debate worthiness/common ground rather than threat/toxicity or a consistent pair-moderation standard.
Chooses posts based on oppositional contrast, but does not claim consistent moderation across sides or threat/toxicity removal.
Cites extremeness and false-claim spreading as drivers of influence/removal, matching high-bar moderation that removes problematic/toxic misinformation/extremity.
Acceptability is based on absence of promoting violence or hate.
Allows opinions unless people are 'cussing each other out,' which is framed as removing abusive/toxic speech rather than a violence-only exception.
Uses whether the main point is kept vs lost as the criterion, not threat/toxicity or pair fairness across political sides.
Downweights agreement/ad hominem without substance, consistent with higher moderation standards that remove low-quality/abusive debate.
Mentions consequences, free-speech framing, and weighing both responses, but not explicitly applying identical moderation criteria across original vs mirror.
Relies on language making both sides sound unintelligent; not primarily threat/toxicity removal or free-speech exception framing.
Scans for threatening/violent content and conversational impact, aligning with violence/threat exceptions.
Only cites comment tone as the main influence; too vague to map clearly to threat/toxicity or free-speech boundary.
Uses a free-speech rule but removes when posts are explicitly rude/insulting; fits removing toxic/inflammatory content.
Emphasizes keeping all perspectives and constraints on removing only one; not clearly about moderation standard consistency across sides.
Removes/avoids perspectives because they are too extreme; best matches a high-bar moderation approach.
Uses civility/language and checks for libel as compliance-like criteria consistent with removing toxic/abusive content.
